comments.author: Simon
comments.post_title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: describe a festival
comments.text:
Hi Alqnas,

Your answers are good. The only thing I disagree with is the band scores next to each answer. These are part 1 questions, so answers should be short and direct. I personally prefer your 'band 5-6' answers (I think you could get a much higher score than 5-6 with those answers IF your part 2 and 3 answers are good).

I've never met a student who was able to give answers like your 'band 7-8' responses. They seem "too perfect" to me, and I wonder why you don't think they are good enough for band 9.

Remember that part 1 is supposed to be easy. You can't get a high score without doing well in parts 2 and 3.

comments.author: Simon
comments.post_title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: describe a festival
comments.text:
Hi Hore boy,

It's not an exact science because it also depends on whether you use the 'less common words/phrases' correctly and in a natural way. I've seen an official IELTS video in which a student only uses 3 or 4 less common phrases and still gets a 7 because he speaks in a fluent, natural way.

The difference between 8 and 9 is quite small, but you can see in the descriptors for band 8 that the student can make some small mistakes in each area: look for the words "occasional inaccuracies", "occasional inappropriacies" or "hesitation to search for language". A band 9 student would speak fluently and naturally, and the only mistakes would be those that a native speaker might make.
